name: LM5060Q1MM_NOPB
title: High-side N-MOSFET protection controller with low quiescent current
summary: The LM5060 controls an external N-channel MOSFET on the high side of a 5.5 V to 65 V rail. A charge pump drives the gate with a constant 24 µA, so the output rises at a nearly fixed rate, and an internal clamp limits VGS to about 16.8 V. It trips on excessive MOSFET drain-source voltage after a delay set by one timer capacitor, latching the MOSFET off; it also has adjustable UVLO with hysteresis, adjustable overvoltage shutdown with automatic restart, an enable input and an open-drain power-good flag. Disabled, it draws 9 µA typical. An automotive grade, LM5060-Q1, is qualified to AEC-Q100.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: Sets the drain-source fault threshold: an internal sink of 16 µA typical draws current through a resistor from the supply side of the MOSFET, so the pin sits below the supply by that resistor's drop.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 5.5 V to 65 V in operation. The power-on reset releases at about 5.1 V. A small ceramic capacitor close to the pin keeps noise off it.

pins.name: OVP
pins.function: Overvoltage comparator input, fed from a divider on the input supply. Above 2.0 V typical the gate is pulled down without latching; the part turns back on once the pin drops under about 1.76 V.

pins.name: UVLO
pins.function: Undervoltage comparator input, fed from a divider between the input supply and ground; active only while EN is high. Above 1.6 V typical the gate pull-downs let go and the output ramps up. A 5.5 µA typical sink holds the pin low when it is left open.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. Under 0.8 V the part drops into its low-current shutdown; over 2.0 V the internal bias and the UVLO comparator start. The gate is charged only when EN and UVLO are both high. A 6 µA typical sink holds the pin low when open.

pins.name: TIMER
pins.function: Fault timing capacitor to ground. When the pin passes 2.0 V the MOSFET is switched off and held off until EN, UVLO or VIN (power-on reset) goes low and back high.

pins.name: nPGD
pins.function: Open-drain status output. It pulls low (no fault) once the MOSFET drain-source voltage has fallen far enough that OUT is above SENSE; otherwise it is high impedance.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Output sense, tied to the output rail at the MOSFET source; used inside to judge VDS and VGS.

pins.name: GATE
pins.function: Gate drive to the external N-channel MOSFET: a charge-pump current source of 24 µA typical. An internal zener holds GATE about 16.8 V above OUT. A capacitor from GATE to ground slows the output ramp.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The simplest arrangement: one N-channel MOSFET Q1 between VIN and VOUT, drain to the input. RS from the input to SENSE sets the drain-source voltage at which a fault is declared. One three-resistor string from VIN to ground gives the UVLO tap above the OVP tap. C1 on TIMER sets the fault delay. R4 pulls the open-drain nPGD up to VIN to make the STATUS line, high on a fault and low when there is none. EN comes in from outside: high turns the switch on.

circuits.title: Basic application circuit
circuits.description: The same switch with UVLO and OVP set by separate dividers, so each threshold can be chosen on its own: R10 over R11 feeds UVLO and R8 over R9 feeds OVP, both from VIN. RS between VIN and SENSE sets the VDS fault level for Q1. C1 on TIMER sets the start-up and fault delays. R4 pulls nPGD up to VIN for the STATUS output.

circuits.title: LM5060EVAL evaluation module
circuits.description: A worked design for 9 V to 37 V and up to 5 A. R4 (9.09 kΩ) from the input to SENSE sets the VDS trip level; R5, a 0 Ω link, takes OUT from the output side of Q1. One string R1, R2, R3 (200 kΩ, 38.3 kΩ, 14.0 kΩ) gives UVLO at 9 V and OVP at 37 V. C1 (0.1 µF) on TIMER sets the fault delays. C3 from GATE to ground is a capacitor that slows the output rise. D1 is a 51 V zener from the input to ground; C4 and C5 (22 µF) sit on the input and output, and C2 (0.1 µF) bypasses VIN. R6 (100 kΩ) pulls nPGD up to the input for STATUS.

circuits.title: Reverse polarity protection with diodes
circuits.description: An automotive switch for 9 V to 24 V and 30 A that withstands a reversed input. Q2, source to source with Q1, keeps Q1's body diode from conducting when VIN is reversed. D3 (36 V zener) limits the input transients produced when Q1 and Q2 shut off quickly; with D2 in series it forms a transient suppressor that keeps reverse voltage stress off input capacitors. D1 protects the VIN pin on a reversed input; C2 bypasses it. R1 (2 kΩ) limits reverse current out of GATE to 25 mA, and D4 bypasses R1 so a fault turn-off stays fast. D6, Q3 and R2 protect Q2 from VGS damage on a reversed input. D5 (OUT to GATE) and D7 (VOUT to SENSE) parallel the internal OUT-to-GATE zener and OUT-to-SENSE diode, which a highly capacitive load and a large reverse input can overstress. R5, R6 and R7 set UVLO at 9 V and OVP at 27 V; R3 sets the VDS trip level and C1 (68 nF) the delays.

operation.text: The LM5060 drives an external N-channel MOSFET on the high side. It protects against overcurrent by watching the voltage across the MOSFET rather than a sense resistor: once that drop exceeds a set threshold for longer than a set time, the MOSFET is turned off. It also watches the input for undervoltage and overvoltage. Pulling EN low turns the MOSFET off and puts the controller in a very low current state. The open-drain nPGD output reports the switch state. Because the gate is charged by a constant current, extra capacitance from GATE to ground stretches the output rise, which suits large capacitive loads.

Start-up begins when EN rises past 2.0 V (with UVLO high and VIN above the power-on reset). The gate charges at 24 µA typical while the timer capacitor charges at 6 µA. When VGS reaches VGATE-TH (5 V typical) the timer capacitor is dumped down to 0.3 V and from there charges at 11 µA. From then the timer runs until either the VDS comparator sees OUT climb above SENSE, which pulls nPGD low and discharges the timer, or the timer reaches VTMRH and a fault is declared.

A charge pump lifts the gate drive above both input and output. With EN and UVLO above threshold, GATE is charged by the 24 µA source; an internal zener keeps GATE no more than about 16.8 V above OUT. With UVLO or EN low, or VIN under the 5.10 V power-on reset, GATE is discharged by a 2.2 mA sink. A timer fault or an overvoltage pulls GATE down with 80 mA.

Three things act on TIMER: a 6 µA source that runs while EN, UVLO and VIN are high; an added 5 µA source (11 µA total) switched in only after the VGS sequence completes; and a pull-down that empties the capacitor whenever EN, UVLO or VIN is low or OVP is high. A VDS fault (SENSE above OUT) releases the pull-down so the capacitor charges. At VTMRH (2 V typical) the gate is discharged at 80 mA and the MOSFET stays latched off until EN, UVLO or VIN is taken low and back high. A timer capacitor is always needed: without enough capacitance the 6 µA reaches 2 V before the gate and output have risen, and the part latches off. Grounding TIMER removes the latch-off altogether (not recommended); nPGD still follows the VDS comparator.

The gate passes from cut-off through the linear region into full enhancement. During the first phase the timer charges at 6 µA; if VGS reaches 5 V first, the timer is reset to 300 mV and charges at 11 µA while the MOSFET finishes turning on. The slower first rate allows more time before a fault. If gate leakage keeps the 24 µA from bringing VGS up to 5 V, the timer reaches 2 V and the gate is discharged at 80 mA. Turn-on time depends on input voltage, load capacitance and resistance, and the MOSFET.

The VDS comparator compares SENSE with OUT. If OUT falls below SENSE, nPGD goes high impedance and the timer charges at 6 µA (VGS under 5 V) or 11 µA (VGS over 5 V); at 2 V the gate is pulled down at 80 mA. The voltage compared is the MOSFET's RDS(ON) drop less the threshold set by RS, so this works as an overcurrent shutdown whose delay is set by CTIMER, ITIMERH and VTMRH. The part suits designs that need some fault protection but not precise current sensing, for example where the impedance or inductance of the supply path itself slows the rise of short-circuit current. The MOSFET safe operating area must cover the peak current for the whole delay, and RDS(ON) spread sets the accuracy of the trip current.
After a VDS fault has run the timer to 2 V the MOSFET is latched off; EN, VIN or UVLO must be taken low and then high to restart.

EN thresholds are CMOS-compatible: below ENTHL (800 mV) the MOSFET turns off, above ENTHH (2.00 V) it turns on; the typical switching point is about 1.5 V with 200 mV of hysteresis. Below about 0.5 V the part enters its low-current disabled state, drawing 9 µA typical from VIN. EN may be driven up to 65 V.

UVLO below threshold turns the MOSFET off with the 2.2 mA GATE sink. A divider from VIN sets the trip point (1.6 V rising, about 180 mV hysteresis at the pin). The pin can serve as a second, redundant shut-down input, but unlike EN it does not put the part into the low-current disabled state. When unused, UVLO is tied to VIN; left floating, its internal pull-down holds the part off. Separately, a power-on reset switches the MOSFET off once VIN drops under about 5.10 V.

When OVP rises above OVPTH (2 V typical) the MOSFET is turned off. A 9.6 µs filter keeps noise from tripping it; an event lasting longer discharges GATE at 80 mA and empties the timer capacitor. Because the timer is reset, the low output that follows does not latch a VDS fault: once OVP falls under about 1.76 V the part restarts through the normal sequence without EN, VIN or UVLO being cycled. When unused, OVP is tied to GND; it is not left floating.

nPGD is open drain and reports VDS faults: with SENSE above OUT it is high impedance, so with a pull-up it reads high during any VDS fault. Its state does not depend on the timer. The pull-up resistor is sized to keep the low-state sink current within 1 mA to 5 mA; it may go to VIN or to any positive supply under 65 V.

A capacitor from GATE to ground slows the output rise. The rise depends on the MOSFET threshold, its gate capacitance and the added capacitance; a slow rise lets the MOSFET charge a large load capacitance gently, but a rise that is too slow can push the MOSFET outside its safe operating area through peak dissipation.

One low-leakage capacitor on TIMER sets both the start-up VGS window and the later overcurrent window, which lets loads such as lamps and motors draw a surge above the trip level for a short time. After start-up the MOSFET may not yet be fully enhanced; VDS must drop below VDSTH before the timer reaches 2 V. A later load surge that trips the VDS comparator lets the 11 µA source charge the capacitor; if it reaches 2 V the gate is discharged at once and the MOSFET latches off. Since one capacitor covers several conditions, its value is a compromise.

BVDSS above the highest system voltage plus ringing and transients at switch-on and switch-off. Transient current rating set by the worst-case VDS fault current. A low threshold voltage keeps the MOSFET in its safe operating area more easily during turn-on, since less gate charge brings it into full conduction. Safe operating area and thermal properties checked against the largest dissipation at start-up or shutdown. RDS(ON) low enough that IL(MAX)² × RDS(ON) keeps the junction within its rating. A MOSFET whose VGS rating is under 16 V needs an external gate-source zener, rated for at least 80 mA forward to carry the full fault pull-down current.

Not every design needs them. When the MOSFET turns off, current falls fast and wiring and trace inductance produce positive spikes on the input and negative spikes on the output. Local capacitance or clamps limit these; the amount needed depends on input voltage, load current, trace inductance and switching speed, and is best settled by measuring the board.

Option A: one string of three resistors (R1, R2, R3) from VIN to ground with UVLO at the upper tap and OVP at the lower. Option B: two independent dividers, R10/R11 on UVLO and R8/R9 on OVP. Option C: OVP grounded and only the UVLO divider fitted. The top resistor of the UVLO divider (R1) or the bottom one (R11, R9) is kept under 100 kΩ; smaller values reduce the effect of UVLOBIAS. UVLO hysteresis is about 180 mV and OVP hysteresis about 240 mV at the pins.

A capacitor between VIN and GND can be required to keep noise and spikes off the supply pin. If Q1 carries a large current, its sudden turn-off can produce an inductive kick large enough to damage the part; a bulk capacitor from VIN to GND, protection diodes or surge suppressors keep VIN, SENSE, OVP, UVLO and nPGD within their ratings.

If the input stays at the output voltage and the load is high impedance when the part turns off, Q1's body diode does not conduct and the load capacitor discharges through the LM5060 at IGATE-FLT, dissipating IGATE-FLT × VOUT at first. With a high input voltage and a very large output capacitor, a resistor RO in series with OUT limits this current; RS must then be recalculated. Where the input can be reversed while a big load capacitor is charged, RO is required to keep current out of OUT under 25 mA. RO and the OUT pin current reduce the accuracy of the VDS threshold.

A second N-channel MOSFET, source to source with the pass device, blocks Q1's body diode on a reversed input. A zener transient clamp on the input catches the spike when both MOSFETs turn off fast; with a series diode it also keeps reversed voltage off the input capacitors. A diode in series with VIN guards the VIN pin. A resistor in the GATE line limits reverse current out of GATE to 25 mA; a diode across it keeps turn-off fast, and it has no effect at turn-on because GATE is a 24 µA source. A small NPN, its base pulled by a resistor and guarded by a diode, protects the second MOSFET's gate on a reversed input. With a highly capacitive load and a large reverse input, current through the internal OUT-to-GATE zener and OUT-to-SENSE diode can exceed their rating: external diodes in parallel with them, or a resistor in series with OUT, carry or limit it.

operation.topic: OUT resistor sizing for reverse polarity
operation.text: A resistor in series with OUT limits current through the internal OUT-to-GATE zener and OUT-to-SENSE diode; the current through the diode between the comparator inputs is held to 4 mA or less, and current into SENSE or OUT from below ground to 25 mA or less. The 8 µA and 16 µA internal sources can be ignored for this. Inside, SENSE connects through 500 Ω and OUT through 1 kΩ to the VDS comparator, with a diode between the two inner nodes and a diode from each pin to ground. Adding RO may call for a change to RS.

The supply range is 5.5 V to 65 V. The source feeding VIN must keep the part within its operating range through all load and line transients. A 10 nF or 100 nF ceramic capacitor sits close to the VIN pin.
Load current runs from the input source straight through the MOSFET to the load on heavy copper. The VIN bypass capacitor sits close to pin 2 and the TIMER capacitor close to pin 7.

In normal operation dissipation is small, typically the input voltage multiplied by an input current of about 2 mA. With a large capacitive load and nothing else to absorb its energy, the load capacitor can discharge back through OUT to ground when the part turns off, for example in a motor drive; the dissipation is then set by the 80 mA discharge current and the capacitor voltage.
